exposure: Maternal free triiodothyronine (FT3) levels in late pregnancy
Maternal free thyroxine (FT4) levels in late pregnancy
Maternal thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels in late pregnancy
cohort: A total of 3757 puerperae who gave birth from September 2019 to October 2020, divided into a case group with low birth weight babies (n=249) and a control group with normal birth weight babies (n=3508).
finding: Decreased maternal free triiodothyronine (FT3) levels and increased free thyroxine (FT4) and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels in late pregnancy significantly raise the risk of singleton low birth weight.
cross-section timing: Maternal thyroid hormone levels were measured in late pregnancy, and clinical data were collected for puerperae who gave birth between September 2019 and October 2020.
birth_weight: Less than 2500g for the case group; greater than 2500g for the control group.
